cell_type_model: mouse kidney/lung single-cell and ischemia-reperfusion models; human AKI serum samples; no S1PR1-specific SPP1 model
assay_or_perturbation: OPN neutralization/knockout, lung-barrier assays, and exact-pair PubMed search; validated OPN targets in the study were CD44/integrin contexts, not S1PR1

pathway_branch: OPN-mediated AKI-ALI function is not assignable to S1PR1; no defensible exact-pair branch

cell_type_model: Human PBMC T- and B-cell single-cell transcriptomic cohorts; no purified pair model
assay_or_perturbation: Single-cell RNA-seq and computational ligand-receptor inference; no biochemical binding, receptor activation, or selective perturbation of SPTAN1/PTPRA
pathway_branch: SPTAN1-PTPRA computationally inferred communication; PTPRA Src-family phosphatase signaling remains a comparator
limitations: The cited primary study reports an inferred communication edge, not direct extracellular SPTAN1-PTPRA binding or activation. SPTAN1 is a cytoskeletal scaffold and PTPRA is a receptor-type phosphatase; pathway/co-expression inference cannot establish a ligand-receptor edge or relay. No exact-pair cell model or terminal TF assay was located.

cell_type_model: Spectrin interactome and neuronal/cytoskeletal comparator systems; no exact SPTBN2-PTPRA extracellular model
assay_or_perturbation: Protein-interaction/co-expression database and spectrinome evidence; no direct ligand binding, receptor activation, or pair-selective perturbation
pathway_branch: spectrin/PTPRA cytoskeletal signaling context; exact SPTBN2-to-PTPRA extracellular branch unresolved
limitations: The spectrinome and co-expression evidence concerns intracellular scaffold associations and does not demonstrate that SPTBN2 is a PTPRA ligand. PTPRA signaling through Src-family kinases cannot be transferred to this exact pair, and no receptor-proximal or downstream functional assay was found.

cell_type_model: Rat brain somatostatin-receptor cloning systems and heterologous SSTR expression; no SST-ADRA2A model
assay_or_perturbation: Somatostatin receptor subtype cloning, ligand binding, and second-messenger characterization; exact ADRA2A assay not established
pathway_branch: SST-SSTR subtype branch; ADRA2A is an adrenergic receptor boundary
limitations: Primary receptor studies support SST action through SSTR subtypes, not ADRA2A. Adrenergic receptor expression or shared Gi/o coupling does not establish SST binding or activation of ADRA2A, and no exact-pair relay or function was identified.

cell_type_model: Somatostatin-receptor and mGlu7 recombinant/neuronal comparator systems; no exact SST-GRM7 model
assay_or_perturbation: SST receptor pharmacology and separate GRM7 glutamate-coupling studies; no exact-pair binding or perturbation
pathway_branch: SST-SSTR and glutamate-GRM7 branches kept separate
limitations: The cited primary literature assigns somatostatin to SSTRs and GRM7 to glutamate pharmacology. GPCR family membership, neuronal co-expression, and convergent Gi/o signaling are not evidence for direct SST-GRM7 interaction or downstream relay.

cell_type_model: Somatostatin-receptor and melatonin-receptor comparator systems; no exact SST-MTNR1A model
assay_or_perturbation: SST receptor subtype cloning/pharmacology and separate melatonin-receptor studies; no exact-pair activation assay
pathway_branch: SST-SSTR branch versus melatonin-MTNR1A branch
limitations: Somatostatin receptor studies do not support MTNR1A as an SST receptor. Circadian/endocrine co-expression or shared GPCR signaling components cannot substitute for an exact ligand-activation assay, and no receptor-proximal or downstream pair evidence was found.

cell_type_model: Mouse ST6Gal1-deficient and Cd22/St6gal1 double-deficient primary B cells; endothelial CD22-ligand display comparator
assay_or_perturbation: St6Gal1 knockout, Cd22 double knockout, CD22-ligand/glycan staining, BCR signaling, endocytosis, and SHP-1 recruitment assays
pathway_branch: ST6GAL1 -> alpha2,6-sialylated glycans -> CD22 engagement -> BCR inhibitory trafficking/signaling
limitations: The primary studies show that ST6GAL1 generates or controls alpha2,6-sialylated CD22 ligands and that CD22 mediates the resulting B-cell phenotype; they do not show ST6GAL1 protein binding to CD22 or a conventional ST6GAL1-initiated receptor relay. Cell-surface glycan context and B-cell specificity are essential, and no terminal TF was directly assigned.

cell_type_model: OV4, SKOV3, BxPC3 and additional epithelial cancer cell models; mouse pancreatic acinar/organoid comparator
assay_or_perturbation: ST6GAL1 overexpression/knockdown, EGFR alpha2,6-sialylation, basal and EGF-induced EGFR phosphorylation, receptor trafficking, AKT/NF-kappaB, and gefitinib-response assays
pathway_branch: ST6GAL1-mediated EGFR sialylation -> EGFR dimerization/activation -> AKT/NF-kappaB and survival/trafficking outputs
limitations: The evidence supports enzymatic modification of EGFR and altered receptor activation, not a conventional ST6GAL1 ligand-receptor binding event. Results are dominated by cancer-cell models and can depend on EGF availability, glycosylation state, and ST6GAL1 expression; no SCI receiver-cell assay or terminal TF occupancy was reported.

cell_type_model: Human vascular/plasma substance-P systems and rat tissue degradation comparator
assay_or_perturbation: DPP4 inhibition, substance-P degradation/inactivation, and vascular/fibrinolytic response assays
pathway_branch: DPP4 cleaves and inactivates substance P, altering the amount of mature peptide available for canonical tachykinin-receptor signaling
limitations: The evidence is direct peptide processing, not DPP4 binding to or activation by a receptor and not a downstream intracellular relay. TAC1 is a precursor that produces multiple mature tachykinins; the cited assays do not establish a TAC1-isoform-specific effect in an SCI cell type or a terminal TF.

cell_type_model: Recombinant human FAP, human peptide/plasma assays, and FAP-active versus FAP-null mouse embryonic fibroblast secretomes
assay_or_perturbation: Purified-enzyme peptide hydrolysis, degradomics/proteomics, and comparison of active/inactive FAP secretomes
pathway_branch: FAP post-proline cleavage of substance P; possible loss or remodeling of mature tachykinin activity
limitations: FAP directly hydrolyzes substance P in biochemical assays, but this is proteolytic processing rather than canonical ligand-receptor activation. FAP substrate usage is context- and sequence-dependent, DPP4 can also process substance P, and no FAP-dependent receptor relay or terminal TF was measured.

cell_type_model: CHO-K1 cells expressing human TACR3; mouse TAC1-derived peptide preparation
assay_or_perturbation: PathHunter beta-arrestin assays with substance P, substance P(6-11), and TAC1-derived capped peptide; plasma stability comparison
pathway_branch: TAC1-derived tachykinin -> TACR3/NK3R -> GPCR beta-arrestin signaling
limitations: TACR3 activation is supported for mature TAC1-derived peptides, including substance P, but the TAC1 gene/precursor and peptide processing were not selectively perturbed in the receptor assay. Potency is lower than for the preferred TACR3 ligand NKB, and no downstream kinase, cell phenotype, or terminal TF was assigned to the exact source annotation.

cell_type_model: Mouse stomach/urinary-bladder smooth-muscle tissues and rat tachykinin-receptor pharmacology systems
assay_or_perturbation: NKB/Tac2-derived peptide agonist and antagonist pharmacology; tissue contraction, receptor subtype discrimination, and Tac2 genetic context
pathway_branch: Tac2/NKB -> TACR1/NK1R cross-reactive tachykinin GPCR branch
limitations: Tac2 encodes NKB in mouse, and NKB can activate NK1/TACR1 at lower potency than its preferred NK3 receptor; however, the cited tissue assays contain mixed receptor populations and do not provide a purified Tac2-TACR1 binding assay. No exact source-cell perturbation or terminal TF was measured.

cell_type_model: Mouse stomach/urinary-bladder smooth-muscle tissues and tachykinin-receptor pharmacology systems
assay_or_perturbation: NKB/Tac2-derived peptide agonist and antagonist pharmacology; receptor subtype potency and Tac2 knockout/reproductive phenotyping
pathway_branch: Tac2/NKB -> TACR2/NK2R cross-reactive tachykinin GPCR branch
limitations: NKB is a lower-potency agonist at TACR2 than NKA, and the tissue assays do not isolate a purified Tac2-TACR2 molecular interaction. Tac2 genetic phenotypes mainly support the Tac2/NKB system rather than this receptor substitution; no downstream TF was directly measured.

cell_type_model: HEK293 cells expressing murine or human NK3/TACR3; no SCI receiver model
assay_or_perturbation: Radioligand/competitive tachykinin receptor binding and agonist-stimulated Ca2+ mobilization in recombinant murine and human NK3 receptor systems
relation_type: Tac2-derived neurokinin B/TACR3 receptor activation; mature-peptide/source-gene mapping retained separately
pathway_branch: Tac2/NKB -> TACR3/NK3R -> GPCR-linked Ca2+ mobilization
limitations: The primary assay tests mature tachykinin agonists in recombinant NK3 systems, not selective Tac2 transcription/processing in an SCI source cell. Species-dependent potency and cross-reactive tachykinin pharmacology remain important; Ca2+ mobilization is receptor-proximal, not terminal-TF evidence.

cell_type_model: Purified human transcobalamin-CD320 structural system and heterologous cannabinoid-receptor expression systems; no exact TCN2-CNR1 model
assay_or_perturbation: TCN2/CD320 structural and binding assays compared with CNR1 cloning/pharmacology; no exact-pair binding, activation, or perturbation
pathway_branch: TCN2 -> CD320 cobalamin uptake branch versus endocannabinoid -> CNR1 branch
limitations: Primary studies identify CD320, not CNR1, as the transcobalamin receptor and identify CNR1 as a cannabinoid receptor. Shared extracellular expression or GPCR/receptor annotation does not establish TCN2-CNR1 binding, receptor-proximal signaling, or pair-specific function.

cell_type_model: HEK293T overexpression/uptake system with human TCN2 variant context; human congenital-heart-defect cohort comparator
assay_or_perturbation: TCN2/holo-transcobalamin uptake comparison by TCN2 variant, cell-associated versus medium protein measurement, and LRP2/megalin siRNA perturbation
relation_type: LRP2-dependent holo-TC uptake/function; direct TCN2-LRP2 binding and intracellular relay not isolated
pathway_branch: TCN2/holo-transcobalamin -> LRP2/megalin -> cellular vitamin-B12 uptake
limitations: The evidence concerns holo-TC uptake and a variant-specific functional difference rather than purified binary binding or a canonical signaling relay. HEK293T overexpression, uptake/reabsorption context, and no SCI receiver model limit transfer; no terminal TF.

cell_type_model: Mouse embryonic tissues, NIH-3T3 stable Tctn1 cells, COS1 co-immunoprecipitation, and hTERT-RPE1 ciliated cells
assay_or_perturbation: TCTN1 co-immunoprecipitation/protein-complex mapping, transition-zone localization, Tctn1/Tmem67 loss-of-function, and ciliogenesis/ciliary-membrane phenotyping
pathway_branch: TCTN1-TMEM67 transition-zone complex -> ciliary membrane composition and tissue-specific ciliogenesis
limitations: The exact TCTN1-TMEM67 association is supported as a ciliary transition-zone complex component, but this is not a secreted ligand-receptor edge or a receptor-proximal intracellular relay. The functional phenotypes are tissue-specific and do not identify a terminal TF or SCI-relevant signaling output.

cell_type_model: Mouse mammary epithelial cells, mammalian receptor-transfection systems, and Xenopus embryonic receptor-reconstitution systems
assay_or_perturbation: Cripto/TDGF1 binding and co-immunoprecipitation with ALK4/ACVR1B, Nodal-dependent SMAD2 reporter/phosphorylation, receptor reconstitution, and dominant-negative perturbation
pathway_branch: Nodal-Cripto/TDGF1-ACVR1B/ActRII complex -> SMAD2/3 branch
limitations: Cripto/TDGF1 is a membrane GPI-anchored co-receptor rather than the canonical Nodal ligand. Direct ALK4 association and Nodal-dependent signaling are supported, but the exact stoichiometry and contribution of ACVR2A versus ACVR2B vary by species and assay; no TDGF1-alone activation or SCI cell-state result was shown.

cell_type_model: Xenopus embryonic and HepG2 receptor-reconstitution systems; human Nodal/Cripto biochemical comparator
assay_or_perturbation: Cripto/TDGF1 interaction with ALK7/ACVR1C, Nodal/Xnr1 receptor reconstitution, co-immunoprecipitation, and dominant-negative embryonic perturbation
pathway_branch: Nodal-Cripto/TDGF1-ACVR1C/ActRIIB complex -> SMAD2/3 branch
limitations: The primary study supports Cripto-enhanced Nodal/ALK7 signaling and direct Cripto-ALK7 association, but receptor use is ligand- and species-dependent and ACVR2B/ActRIIB is part of the functional complex. No TDGF1-alone activation, SCI model, or terminal TF occupancy was established.

cell_type_model: Human Nodal/Cripto biochemical systems and Xenopus/mouse Nodal-receptor comparator systems; no isolated TDGF1-ACVR2A model
assay_or_perturbation: SPR/co-immunoprecipitation and receptor-reconstitution studies of Nodal, Cripto, ALK4/ALK7, and ActRII receptors
pathway_branch: Nodal-ACVR2A/ACVR2B type-II receptor branch; direct TDGF1-ACVR2A edge unresolved
limitations: Nodal binds type-II receptors and Cripto participates in Nodal complexes, but the primary assays do not establish a direct TDGF1/Cripto-ACVR2A interaction or a TDGF1-initiated relay. Cripto can alter Nodal receptor binding without being the canonical ligand, and receptor-complex analogy was not used to promote this exact pair.
